minutes.headline: Commission approved a deck, septic and patio permits, a field change and Kelly funds for title searches; a stop-work order stays.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission met by Zoom, approved two sets of minutes, and ruled on several hearings, approving a deck RDA, two septic/patio NOIs and a field change. Many hearings were continued to 12/20. The commission discussed the 711 Mass Ave cease-and-desist, the Hollis Road lease, tree-protection interpretation, and a recruitment push for a new commissioner.

public_comment.topic: Chair invited public comment at the opening; no hands were raised.
No public questions on the 64 Spring Street Extension deck RDA.
Attendees stated why they stayed: watching the process, and the 7-Eleven/Mass Ave and 255 Sunny Hill Road matters; one neighbor of Sunny Hill Road recalled his earlier objection.
Closing call for public comment; none.

votes.outcome: passed 5-0 (unanimous, four roll-call votes plus chair)

votes.motion: Negative determination with standard conditions for deck RDA at 64 Spring Street Extension
Approve NOI for septic replacement at 85 Chase Road with standard order of conditions
Approve NOI for 10 Sunset Avenue with standard order of conditions
Continue 255 Sunny Hill Road NOI to 12/20
Approve field change at 406 Sunset Lane (recessed granite steps) as proposed
Use Kelly estate funds for title searches on three tax-title properties
Authorize Mike to contact a contractor to service the Hollis Road heating system if the facilities director declines

budget_items.what_was_said: The tenant is on month-to-month after the lease expired and pays below market, with volunteer hours undocumented. Rent goes into a revolving fund for that property.

budget_items.topic: Kelly estate funds for title searches
budget_items.what_was_said: A purchase order was to be generated from the Kelly estate fund, with more added if searches cost more.
Unclear what a purchase order covered and how much remains for training; the administrator is to follow up with accounting.

budget_items.topic: Grants and local match for Lane property trail work
budget_items.what_was_said: Snow Riders grant work is well underway and vendor donation receipts and staged gravel may count toward the local match.
A forester earns a percentage of timber sales; no update on whether the Raino property will be logged.

decisions.decision: Town beach appointment hearing by Parks moved to the 12/20 meeting at the Parks chair's request.
At 711 Mass Ave the cease-and-desist stays until the applicant corrects the silt fence, locates missing wetland flags and provides a restoration plan; a site walk will follow.
Administrator to contact the 780 Northfield Road owner about a friendly enforcement order and place him on the 12/20 agenda.
Bob to consult town counsel about the Hollis Road lease and report back with options.
Administrator to print wetlands brochures and post them in Town Hall, the Ritter building and similar spots; QR code link waits on website cleanup.
Commissioners favored holding a separate workshop rather than adding training to regular meetings.
Heating service at Hollis Road goes on the next agenda; Mike will check with the facilities director first.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a deck permit, two septic and patio permits and a field change, and spent town funds on title searches.
The Commission voted to use Kelly estate funds for title searches on three tax-title properties.
At 711 Mass Ave the cease-and-desist stays until the applicant fixes the silt fence, locates missing wetland flags and provides a restoration plan.
Seven hearings, including 390 Howard Street and three Kilburn Street lots, were continued to the 12/20 meeting.
On the Hollis Road lease, a member is to consult town counsel and report back with options; heating service was authorized if the facilities director declines.

why_it_matters: The commission's permits decide what can be built near wetlands in Lunenburg, and the stop-work order at 711 Mass Ave shows the conditions it will hold a project to.
The Hollis Road house is town-owned property whose lease is month-to-month at a below-market rent as heard, so counsel's advice may change what that property earns for its revolving fund.
watch_next: The 12/20 Conservation Commission meeting, where the continued hearings, the town beach appointment hearing and the 780 Northfield Road owner are on the agenda.
Town counsel's options on the Hollis Road lease, due back to the commission.

The official minutes record many administrator follow-ups, the Richard Bursch absence and the public comment, and ours does not. The 711 Mass Ave and 780 Northfield Road decisions are worded differently in the two records and should be checked against the recording.
